title: An empty `--diff` with `-o` leaves yesterday's pack in place as today's answer
evidence: When `--diff` selects nothing, the command exits 0 and writes nothing (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:712`-`714`); with `-o FILE`, "a pack from an earlier run is left in place, where a caller may read it as current". This sits against the business claim "The same request always produces the same file, so two reviewers... see the same thing" and "It never quietly drops content."
failure: A scheduled job runs `sealmap pack --diff main -o review.txt` nightly. On a no-change night the previous pack — built from a different selection and an older revision — is served to the reviewer or agent, who treats it as the current diff's evidence. The wrong topics get reviewed and the changed ones do not.

title: Pack provenance cannot distinguish different uncommitted states, and reports "unknown" outside git
evidence: The revision line is `HEAD` plus `+dirty` when tracked files differ, "not how" (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:769`-`770`, marked Tension); untracked files do not make it dirty (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:763`-`769`); outside a repository the revision is simply `unknown` (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:767`-`770`). The pack is positioned as review evidence whose header carries custody.
failure: Two packs produced from different uncommitted edits carry byte-identical headers. An auditor comparing headers — the thing the header exists for — concludes two different reviews examined the same state. From a tarball export, every pack is labelled `unknown` and provenance is lost entirely.
marked_by_authors: yes (Tension) for `+dirty`; the `unknown`-revision and untracked-file gaps are unmarked
